endorsements.quote: Regulatory approval should then be obtained.

To improve clinical translation and acceptance of AI technologies, researchers need to clearly define the intended use, show transparency in their methodology to allow for reproducibility, demonstrate clinical safety, and clearly state the role of the AI technology in current clinical practice.

It is always important to assess the robustness of AI algorithms using a pre-set operating threshold (on the training/validation datasets) to evaluate it on the local or international testing datasets using performance metrics such as the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, specificity and 95% confidence interval.

unlisted_practices: Use AI reporting guidelines (STARD-AI, TRIPOD-AI, DECIDE-AI, SPIRIT-AI, CONSORT-AI) at the appropriate stage of AI development and clinical translation.
Define the intended use and intended use environment of an AI tool at the start of development.
Engage early with technology transfer or IP offices and regulatory bodies when developing AI.
Address intellectual property issues before publishing AI algorithms.
Engage key stakeholders including patients, clinicians, and policymakers in AI implementation.
Conduct health economic analyses of AI technologies to support policy-level acceptance.
Evaluate the impact of widely adopted AI on population health and society.

screen.reason: This is a commentary proposing a structured approach to utilizing AI reporting guidelines to support clinical translation and implementation.
